text: Geographic tests create the risk of a no man's land transaction: defendants may persuade the courts of every jurisdiction that the transaction took place outside their borders, leaving the transaction governed by no law and with no available forum.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Richard W. Painter, Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2029983

isBasedOn.name: Forum Competition and Choice of Law Competition in Securities Law after Morrison v. National Austral

abstract: Alternatively, defendants might successfully persuade courts in all jurisdictions that a transaction took place outside their borders or for some other reason outside their jurisdictions. Such a "no man's land" transaction would be governed by no law and there would be no forum.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: transactions whose geographic location is ambiguous
courts in all candidate jurisdictions apply geographic tests
